name: Gas-fired packaged fire-tube (shell) steam boiler
description: Shop-assembled shell boiler with the burner firing into a large furnace tube and hot gas making two to four passes through tubes surrounded by boiler water; the standard packaged steam source for small and medium gas-fired industrial loads. Wet-back reversal chambers give more heating surface than refractory-lined dry-back designs.

specifications.basis: Spirax Sarco: 'a compromise is reached with a furnace tube wall thickness of between 18 mm and 20 mm'
Spirax Sarco: that tube wall thickness 'translates to a practical pressure limit for shell boilers of around 27 bar'; most operate at 17 bar or less

specifications.metric: gas temperature before reversal chamber, plain steel
specifications.basis: Spirax Sarco: gas should be cooled to at least 420 C before entering the reversal chamber of a plain-steel shell boiler

specifications.metric: gas temperature before reversal chamber, alloy steel
specifications.basis: Spirax Sarco: 470 C minimum for alloy-steel construction
Spirax Sarco: flame temperature 'may be up to 1800 C'
CBEX packaged firetube: 100-2,500 HP, steam to 300 psig, hot water to 125 psig, 2- or 3-pass
CBLE four-pass packaged firetube: 50-800 HP, steam to 300 psig
CBLE offers NOx ratings down to 5 ppm on natural gas (vendor options)

applications: process steam for food, chemical and manufacturing plants

gaps.what: turndown and part-load efficiency curves for the main gas fire-tube lines
gaps.why: Vendor pages read give output, pressure and NOx but not turndown for CBEX/CBLE.
gaps.next_action: Read distributor specification sheets for turndown data.
